purpose: fn-34 beech and birch protocol profiles. Ash is gathered but unready and is not in this runner set.

fresh_seeds.draw: After initial calibration commits, use OS cryptographic random unsigned 32-bit integers; reject only duplicate/fixed seeds. Write all seeds before generating any. Never replace a failed seed.
fresh_seeds.record: Commit seed list and calibration commit before further tuning; retain failed specimens as regressions.

definitions.height_m: Maximum Y of actual wood/retained foliage above root ground Y=0; exclude root flare below ground. Also report wood-only height. Envelope height is a parameter, not a measurement.
definitions.dbh_m: Diameter at 1.3 m above root ground along dominant trunk, interpolating intersecting structural edge radii; report 2*radius as circular-equivalent centreline model proxy. Multi-stem at this plane is ambiguous and must be flagged, not summed. Sources using US breast height (~1.37 m) are approximate comparisons; retain measurement height.
definitions.crown_width_m: Maximum of X and Z retained-foliage AABB spans; also report both spans. Approximation to field maximum spread; do not use wood buttress or envelope width.
definitions.crown_base_m: Lowest retained foliage Y above ground; report live primary-branch insertion separately. Hanging foliage and branch insertion are different.
definitions.foliage_length_m: Base-to-tip longitudinal extent of each transformed blade or needle, excluding separately modeled petiole/peg; use actual geometry, not unscaled parameter. Report min/max and median.
definitions.foliage_width_m: Maximum blade width transverse to midrib; needle width is maximum cross-section span, not its length or its projected screen width.
definitions.branch_count: Biological axes beginning at forks, excluding trunk. Collapse degree-two chains; choose thickest child as axis continuation, tie-break by stable node index. Report this operational estimate separately from stored branch-run count and nodes.
definitions.branch_order: Trunk order 0; continuing dominant axis retains order, lateral at fork increases it by one. Histogram counts branch origins, not all nodes.
definitions.twig_count: Unique retained twig runs (NodeKind::Twig), each a terminal fine woody axis; does not imply one leaf.
definitions.foliage_units: Beech: one simple entire blade per instance. Always report units_per_instance, pre-cull instances, retained instances, actual individual units and discarded units.
definitions.leaf_area_m2: Sum transformed triangle areas once for a single blade sheet; do not double for double-sided rendering. Neither is field occupancy.

profiles.context: Mature tree-form, healthy leaf-on, open-grown European parkland or woodland-edge; adequate site, no hedge, pollard, purple/weeping/columnar cultivar or closed-forest suppressed bole. Winter image is branch and bark anatomy only. Growth traits are copied from the oak; age 120 yr is set so the mature reference height of 32 m is met. Full growth-trait calibration through time waits for fn-30.

height_m.note: Packham et al. 2012: often 30-40 m, occasionally 50 m in near-natural stands. Houston Durrant, de Rigo & Caudullo (European Atlas of Forest Tree Species): commonly 30-40 m, to 50 m. Gating is the mature typical, not the 50 m exceptional. OSU landscape 15-23 m is contextual and is not substituted.

dbh_m.note: Trees and Shrubs Online: to 1(-1.3?) m dbh. Packham stand diameters (0.14-0.22 m) are younger forest cohorts and are not this context. 1.3 m model plane; sources do not always state measurement height.

crown_width_m.note: OSU landscape spread 12-18 m on 15-23 m trees. Open-grown park trees can be broader; no forest-mature crown-width distribution located. Not a pass claim.

crown_width_height_ratio.note: Engineering estimate from OSU landscape height/spread. Labelled estimate; not a measured population interval.

crown_base_m.note: Open-grown beech often retains low limbs; forest trees clean the bole. No context-matched range located.

foliage_length_m.note: Packham 4-10 cm; OSU 5-10 cm. Packham trimmed-hedge leaves to 16 cm are excluded from this context.

foliage_width_m.note: TSO (3-)4-10 x 2.5-4 cm; JRC typically 10 x 7 cm. Union of cited widths; no joint length-width distribution.

branch_count.note: No context-matched biological range located; report actual value without a pass claim.

branch_order.note: No context-matched biological range located; report actual value without a pass claim.

twig_count.note: No context-matched biological range located; report actual value without a pass claim.

foliage_units.note: No context-matched biological range located; report actual value without a pass claim.

leaf_area_m2.note: No context-matched biological range located; report actual value without a pass claim.

anatomy.element: Single entire ovate-to-elliptic blade, acute tip, wavy or remotely fine-toothed margin, 5-9 vein pairs, visible short petiole; no lobes. One simple blade per instance.
anatomy.attachment: Alternate, two-ranked individual leaves along the local twig; blade bases connect by petiole, not floating clusters.
anatomy.branching: Usually single-stemmed; open-grown crown dense, pyramidal becoming oval or rounded, low limbs retained; smoother and less crooked than the oak. Natural regularity must remain possible with supernatural effects disabled.

rubric.crown_silhouette: Dense oval-to-rounded outline, not a narrow spruce cone and not the oak's irregular windows; B-WHOLE.
rubric.branching_habit: Substantial bole into a regular scaffold; winter limbs smoother than oak; B-BARE.
rubric.crown_gaps: Deep shade, few large interior windows; B-WHOLE.
rubric.terminal_taper: Thick limbs reduce to fine twigs without abrupt stumps; B-BARE.
rubric.foliage_shape_attachment: Entire ovate blades, alternate, short petiole visible at detail scale; B-LEAF, B-LEAVES.
rubric.bark: Smooth silver-grey, elephant-hide on old trunks; B-BARE.

profiles.context: Mature tree-form, healthy leaf-on, open-grown European parkland or woodland-edge; not a cutleaf, purple or weeping cultivar ('Youngii', 'Laciniata'), not a multi-stem coppice stool. Winter image is branch and bark anatomy only. Growth traits are copied from the oak; age 70 yr is set so the mature reference height of 18 m is met. Full growth-trait calibration through time waits for fn-30.

height_m.note: OSU landscape 12-15(24) m; Trees and Shrubs Online usually 10-15 m, to 25 m; JRC Atlas and Atkinson 1992 to 30 m. Gating is mature open-grown typical, not the 30 m exceptional forest maximum.

dbh_m.note: Estimate. No context-matched mature open-grown DBH table located in Atkinson 1992, TSO or OSU. Birch is a slender-boled species; this interval is labelled and cannot gate.

crown_width_m.note: Pyramidal becoming rounded; no cited spread distribution for the species form.

crown_width_height_ratio.note: Engineering estimate around a lighter, narrower crown than beech. Labelled estimate.

crown_base_m.note: No context-matched biological range located; report actual value without a pass claim.

foliage_length_m.note: OSU 2.5-7.5 cm; TSO 50-75 mm; Flora of North America 3-7 cm.

foliage_width_m.note: TSO 45-60 mm; FNA 2.5-5 cm. Doubly serrate deltoid blade; serration is not a lobe count.

anatomy.element: Single deltoid-to-rhombic ovate blade, acuminate tip, coarsely doubly serrate, truncate to cuneate base, long slender petiole; no lobes. One simple blade per instance.
anatomy.attachment: Alternate individual leaves along the local twig; long petiole (TSO 20-30 mm) connects blade to twig.
anatomy.branching: Slender bole; branches upright with thin pendulous outer branchlets on older trees; light open crown. White bark, dark markings at branch junctions. Natural pendulous fine twigs must remain possible with supernatural effects disabled.

rubric.crown_silhouette: Pyramidal becoming rounded, lighter than beech, a haze of fine twigs; S-WHOLE.
rubric.branching_habit: Pendulous outer branchlets; winter silhouette airy; S-BARE.
rubric.crown_gaps: Open, not a solid beech shell; S-WHOLE.
rubric.terminal_taper: Fine hanging twigs, not oak-heavy limbs; S-BARE.
rubric.foliage_shape_attachment: Deltoid doubly-serrate blades, alternate, long petiole; S-LEAF, S-SHOOT.
rubric.bark: White, dark chevrons at junctions; older base darker; S-BARK.
